Layout Patterns

  • Page shells drawn only from the three reference apps (see SKILL.md → "Survey of the repo").
  • Pick the closest match below. Don't design a new page structure from scratch.
  • Ask, don't assume: the mapping table at the bottom covers common resource shapes, but a real backend may expose more than one shape (e.g. a collection and a live stream). If the primary landing view isn't obvious, ask the user — redoing this later is expensive.

1. App Shell — sidebar + header + routed content (Stack A)

Source: visual-pipeline-and-platform-evaluation-tool/ui/src/components/Layout.tsx + Navigation.tsx

Sidebaricon nav, collapsible to icon-only
Headersidebar-trigger | separator | page title | theme toggle (fixed 60px)
Main contentReact Router <Outlet/>, scrollable, flex h-full overflow-auto
  • Toaster (top-center) + a persistent "background jobs" widget overlay the whole shell.
  • Active nav item gets a border-r-3 brand-colored accent.
  • Main content area: each route owns its own internal scrolling.
  • Use for any stack-A app with more than one page/section. Don't add a sidebar to a single-page app.

2. Dashboard Grid — content + side info panel (Stack A "Home" page)

Source: visual-pipeline-and-platform-evaluation-tool/ui/src/pages/Home.tsx

Main regionflex-1 overflow-auto, p-4, space-y-8 — summary cards, list/table sections
Side panelw-86, border-l, bg-sidebar — secondary/glanceable info (quick stats, recent items)
  • Side panel: fixed width, sidebar-tinted background. Secondary content only, never primary.
  • Default shape for a stack-A "overview/operations" landing page.

3. Dashboard with left panel + live right panel (Stack B)

Source: education-ai-suite/smart-classroom/ui/src/components/common/Body.tsx

Top panelscreen switcher + conditional HeaderBar
Left panelcontent/controls
Right panelanalytics/results, collapsible via center arrow divider
Footer
  • No URL routing — local activeScreen state union ('main' | 'content-search' | 'grading' | ...); tool/full-screen states replace the body, not a route.
  • Right panel collapses via a draggable divider (usePanelDividerX hook) to flex: 0.
  • Responsive: @media (max-width: 900px) stacks to a single column.
  • Reports/history are slide-over panels over the whole workspace, not separate pages. Z-index: header 50, toast 1100, video 1000, modal 9999.
  • Use for a "process something, then show results alongside it" app (e.g. upload → transcript/summary/mindmap tabs).

4. Split Panel — config/control card + live preview (Stack C)

Source: live-video-captioning/app/ui/index.html + styles.css (.panels grid)

Topbartitle | device/capability cards | chat toggle | theme toggle
Config cardleft: form controls + nested system-stats-card
Live layoutright: run cards, video/caption panels, empty-state hint
  • CSS grid: grid-template-columns: minmax(300px, 27%) minmax(0, 1fr); — left is a fixed ~27%/min-300px config panel, right takes the rest and is the primary visual focus.
  • Right side renders one run card per active session/stream; shows .empty-alert when nothing is running.
  • Optional slide-over chat panel (RAG assistant), docked right, toggled from the header: <section class="chat-panel"> with a backdrop + dialog + iframe — not a modal library.
  • Use for any live feed/recording/session app (video, audio, sensor stream) with config controls alongside it.

Responsive rules (all three stacks)

  • Stack A: sidebar collapses to icon-only (never hidden); main content keeps independent scrolling at all widths.
  • Stack B: two-panel workspace collapses to a single stacked column below 900px.
  • Stack C: left column has a minmax(300px, 27%) floor. No documented breakpoint below that — ask the user if it matters for their target devices before inventing one.

Choosing a layout for a new resource

Backend resource shapeStack AStack BStack C
Collection/list with CRUD (cameras, rules, documents) App Shell page + Dashboard Grid Left panel list/table inside the left-panel slot Config card (left) listing/selecting items
Single long-lived session/stream (video, audio, sensor) Dashboard Grid main region, or a dedicated route Right-panel live view (video/transcript) Split Panel (right side = live run)
Multi-page app with distinct sections App Shell (sidebar nav) Screen-state switch (activeScreen), no router Not applicable — single-page. Recommend stack A if the app needs to grow multi-page.
Small single-purpose operational dashboard Dashboard Grid — Split Panel
